question: What is the role of a learning rate in gradient descent?
model_answer: It controls the size of each update step: too large overshoots or diverges and too small converges very slowly.
student_answer: It decides how big a step we take in the direction of the negative gradient. If it is too big the loss can blow up.

question: What does dropout do during training?
model_answer: It randomly sets a fraction of activations to zero at each step so the network cannot rely on any single unit; this acts as regularisation.
student_answer: It randomly turns off some neurons in each iteration which reduces overfitting.
